question.text: A 'unified structure' for an AIF is used when:

answer.text: Only one investor participates in the fund
Offshore capital is routed into the domestic SEBI-registered AIF, so offshore and domestic corpus is aggregated into the domestic AIF
The fund invests in only one company
All investors are from the same country

explanation.text: The Logic: In a unified structure (pp. 106-108), offshore fund capital is routed into the domestic SEBI-registered AIF, aggregating offshore and domestic corpus into the domestic AIF rather than the offshore fund investing directly into Indian investee companies in parallel. The Trap: Option A confuses unified structure with single-investor funds. Option C describes a single-investee fund. Option D describes investor geography rather than the pooling arrangement. Note: The workbook table for unified structure still shows two pooling vehicles, so it is incorrect to describe the unified structure as having only one fund vehicle. The defining feature is the aggregation of offshore capital into the domestic AIF.
